title: Caring for Guests
note: This is caring for guests, expected and unexpected. He ranks it first among household duties, and places it after loving-kindness because only two people joined by loving-kindness can do it.

couplets.plain: The whole point of staying at home and keeping things up is to care for guests and do them good.
couplets.pm: All the work of staying at home with your wife, not going to the forest, and looking after your wealth, is so that you can care for guests and help them. Without that help, staying at home and the toil of earning wealth have no use.

links.quote: to care for guests and do them good
links.reason: Makes caring for the guest the very reason for keeping a home.

couplets.plain: To eat while your guest stays outside is not to be wished for, even if it is the medicine against death.
couplets.pm: Even if what you eat is ambrosia, you shouldn’t want to eat it alone while a guest who came to you stays outside your home. It can also be read: even if some call eating once without a guest a medicine against death, leave it. These two couplets tell the excellence of caring for guests.

links.quote: To eat while your guest stays outside
the medicine against death
links.reason: Picks the medicine against death to show what one should still not eat alone.

links.quote: your guest stays outside
links.reason: The guest left outside decides what the host may eat.

couplets.plain: The life of one who cares for the guests who come each day will not suffer and fall to ruin.
couplets.pm: The home life of one who cares every day for the guests who come to him isn’t ruined by the misery of poverty. His wealth doesn’t shrink by this but grows more and more.

links.quote: will not suffer and fall to ruin
links.reason: Promises freedom from ruin to the one who cares for guests each day.

links.quote: the guests who come each day
links.reason: Concerns the guests who come each day, who must always be cared for.

couplets.plain: With a glad heart the goddess of fortune lives in the home of one who cares for good guests with a glad face.
couplets.pm: The goddess of fortune lives gladly in the home of one who cares for worthy guests with a pleasant face. She is glad because her wealth is going the right way. Worthy means high in knowledge and conduct. This gives the reason why his wealth grows.

links.quote: cares for good guests with a glad face
links.reason: A glad face for guests is what brings fortune in to stay.

links.quote: the goddess of fortune lives in the home
links.reason: The goddess of fortune herself moves in with such a host.

couplets.plain: Need you even sow seed in the field of one who feeds guests and eats what is left?
couplets.pm: Does the field of one who first feeds his guests and then eats what is left even need seed sown? No. It yields by itself. These three couplets tell what those who care for guests gain in this life.

links.quote: feeds guests and eats what is left
sow seed in the field

couplets.plain: One who looks after the guest who is leaving and watches for the guest still to come is a good guest to those in the sky.
couplets.pm: One who has tended the guests who came, and then watches for those still to come so as to eat with them, becomes a god in his next birth and a good guest to those in the sky. A good guest means one they seldom get. This tells the reward in the next world.

links.quote: a good guest to those in the sky
links.reason: The host who never stops receiving will be received in his turn by those in the sky.

links.quote: the guest who is leaving

couplets.plain: There is no saying how great the fruit of the sacrifice is. It is measured by the worth of the guest.
couplets.pm: The reward of the sacrifice of caring for guests has no fixed measure. Its only measure is the worth of the guest. It is called a sacrifice because it is one of the five great sacrifices. The amount given doesn’t decide it, since a small gift in worthy hands grows huge. This is why it brings reward in both worlds.

links.quote: It is measured by the worth of the guest

couplets.plain: After anxious guarding they will say “We have nothing to hold on to”: those who never took up the sacrifice of caring for guests.
couplets.pm: Those without the good fortune to care for guests with their wealth and gain the reward of sacrifice guard that passing wealth with pain, then lose it and lament, “Now we have no support.” Even guarding wealth is hard pain, so he says they guarded it anxiously.

links.quote: never took up the sacrifice of caring for guests
links.reason: Shows the cost of never caring for guests: anxious guarding and nothing left to hold.

links.quote: We have nothing to hold on to
links.reason: Speaks in the voice of one who guarded what they had and ended with nothing to hold.

couplets.plain: Poverty amid plenty is the folly of neglecting guests. It is found among fools.
couplets.pm: Poverty in a time of plenty is the stupidity that scorns caring for guests. It isn’t found in those who know, only in fools. It loses what wealth is for and so turns having into not having. Even if the wealth stays, it is useless. These two couplets tell the fault of not caring for guests.

links.quote: the folly of neglecting guests
links.reason: Calls neglecting guests a poverty that no amount of plenty can cover.

links.quote: Poverty amid plenty
It is found among fools

couplets.plain: The aṉiccam flower wilts when you smell it. A guest wilts when you look at them with a changed face.
couplets.pm: The aṉiccam flower wilts only when smelled. Guests wilt when looked at with a changed face. A host needs a pleasant face from afar, sweet words as they come near and good deeds once they accept. Without the first, they wilt and leave while still far off, so guests are more delicate than the flower. A pleasant face comes first.

links.quote: A guest wilts when you look at them with a changed face
flower wilts when you smell it
links.reason: The flower that wilts at a sniff is the measure of a guest.

links.quote: A guest wilts
links.reason: Describes the guest and how little it takes to make them wilt.
